sections.html:
Greenville anchors the Upstate, sitting in Blue Ridge foothills between Atlanta and Charlotte, with the Reedy River cutting through downtown. Headcount climbed from 58,409 in 2010 to 70,720 in 2020, up 21.1 percent. Roughly a million people live in the metro area.

No single employer props up the local economy, since manufacturing, healthcare, banking and logistics all hire here. So a Greenville house that lingers on the market usually has a house-specific problem: condition, title, tenants or timing. Neighborhoods ringing downtown include the Village of West Greenville, the West End, Cleveland Park and Southernside. Spots within reach of Falls Park and the Swamp Rabbit Trail get plenty of attention from buyers.

sections.h2: Tax bills, due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Real estate tax notices from Greenville County arrive in late October. The Tax Collector's counter is at 301 University Ridge, Suite S-1100, and the line is 864-467-7050. Walk-in hours run 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

DateWhat happens to a real property bill
On or after October 1Tax notices issued
January 15Due with no penalty; last day to apply for the 4 percent legal residence rate
After January 153 percent added
After February 110 percent added
After March 1615 percent added

January 1 is the county's record date. Should a house sell after it, you may see both the old and new owners' names on that year's bill, and the following year's bill lists only the current owner.

Only owner-occupied homes get the 4 percent legal residence rate, which carries a credit wiping out the school operation tax. If you have already moved away, you probably do not qualify. Bills left unpaid can land a property in the county tax sale, held at the Greenville Convention Center, 1 Exposition Drive, with bidder registration required 30 days or more in advance.

sections.h2: What a sale does to the next owner's assessment
sections.html:
A closed sale may be classed by the county as an assessable transfer of interest. The house is then valued afresh at market, using a December 31 appraisal date for the year of sale, and the 15 percent cap no longer limits that increase. If the new value rises, the notice typically gives 90 days to appeal.

Put simply, your buyer's bill could exceed yours. Buyers often ask what they will owe, so phone the Assessor or Auditor before you list.

Recording happens at the Register of Deeds, 301 University Ridge, Suite S-2100 (864-467-7240), Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Show up before 4:30. Clerks do not draft deeds or other documents, so finish those first. The office's recording page links a transfer tax calculator and a list of exemptions.

The recording charge is $1.85 on the first $500 of value, then $1.30 per additional $500, as laid out on the Department of Revenue page.

South Carolina's Supreme Court counts deed drafting, title work and closing supervision as practicing law, which is why an attorney there conducts every closing. You must also give the buyer a written property condition disclosure before signing a contract unless the sale is exempt. Sales by estate fiduciaries and transfers between spouses are among the exemptions in state law.

sections.h2: Short-term rentals, permits and code issues
sections.html:
City rules for short-term rentals depend on a property's zoning classification. They arrived after more residents started listing homes on Airbnb and VRBO. Anyone planning to rent a house by the night should confirm the zoning first.

Also ask the city whether the property has open permits or code complaints. Closing those out before a sale means paperwork will not hold up the closing.

sections.h2: Why buyers want to be near downtown
sections.html:
Downtown Greenville gives agents plenty to point to. Falls Park on the Reedy has the Liberty Bridge and waterfalls. The Peace Center for the Performing Arts, the Greenville County Museum of Art, the 16,000-seat Bon Secours Wellness Arena and Fluor Field at the West End, home of the Greenville Drive, are all close. The 22-mile Swamp Rabbit Trail runs through the city, and 4.5 miles were added in 2023.

If your house is a short walk or ride from any of these, say so in the first line of your listing or when you speak with a cash buyer. If it is farther out, interstate access matters more: I-85 runs along the southeast edge of the city, with I-185 and I-385 connecting to downtown. Either way, the pitch should match where the house really sits.

Greenville buyers often ask how far a house is from the airport, the interstate and downtown. US 123, US 25, US 29 and US 276 all serve the city. Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport, over in Greer, is the state's third busiest. Greenlink runs the local buses, and Amtrak's Crescent stops at the city's train station. Pilots may also care that Greenville Downtown Airport is the state's busiest for general aviation, and Michelin and BMW arrived in the area in 1984 and 1994, which is why many newcomers search the Upstate.

The Greenville County School District covers the entire city, and it is the largest in South Carolina. Buyers who ask about a particular school should get the zone for your address from the district office, not from a listing sheet.

Around 47 to 50 inches of rain fall in a typical year, so drainage gets noticed. After a heavy storm, tour your lot and mark where puddles linger. Inspectors spot these within minutes. Service receipts for the furnace and air conditioner belong in the same folder.

Pull together what the closing attorney will need: your deed, newest tax bill, any permit paperwork, the lender's payoff letter and the disclosure form. Compare the owners named on the deed with the people who will actually sign. Tenants in place? Make copies of each lease and note when it ends.

sections.h2: Selling a house that needs repairs
sections.html:
Greenville owners can hire an agent, go it alone or accept an offer in cash. Putting the house on the market tends to bring the best price when it is in good shape. Cash makes more sense for a place needing work, one with tenants, or a sale that has to close by a set date. Cash buyers take the property as is, so you avoid repair requests and lender delays, though their offer will reflect the repairs.

Whichever you choose, the closing involves a South Carolina attorney and the Register of Deeds. The attorney pays off your mortgage and any tax owed from the proceeds, then records the deed.

Mind the calendar: a spring closing leaves the buyer holding a new bill later that year, while a winter closing may land when taxes are already due. Have the attorney show how the tax split will read on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: When are Greenville County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by January 15 to avoid penalties. Late payments pick up 3 percent first, 10 percent once February 1 passes and 15 percent after March 16. Bills are issued starting October 1.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Greenville?
faqs.a: Take it to the Greenville County Register of Deeds, 301 University Ridge, Suite S-2100, Greenville, SC 29601. The phone is 864-467-7240, and the office wants you in the door by 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the buyer's tax bill change after a sale in Greenville County?
faqs.a: Possibly. If the sale counts as an assessable transfer of interest, the house is revalued at current market and the 15 percent cap is lifted for that transfer.

faqs.q: Why is the prior owner's name on the tax bill?
faqs.a: The county records ownership as of January 1. A house that changes hands afterward can show both owners on that year's bill, then only the new one the next year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenville house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, we purchase houses in any condition. Closing still goes through a South Carolina attorney and the Register of Deeds. Describe the property and we will explain what we can offer.
